correctness.rationale: The six-vertex class and query domain are fully explicit. Direct exhaustive enumeration of all 2^15 edge orientations yields exactly 2640 legal score patterns; testing all 2^15 supports gives the complete polynomial and excludes higher support sizes. Independent cut inequality classification agrees on all 32768 cases. All 1185 maximum supports are canonically classified under all 720 label permutations. An explicit 2048-leaf depth-eleven tree certifies the online lower bound, and 2640<4096 certifies the upper bound. The general cut lemma follows rigorously by prescribed-degree flow orientation.

The previous regular-seven support polynomial aggregates supports touching and avoiding the deleted vertex, so it does not imply the separate six-vertex coefficientwise counts or extremal isomorphism spectrum.

value.rationale: Near-regular tournament scores are a classical natural even-order counterpart to regular tournaments (Brualdi–Kiernan 2009). The six-vertex case supplies the first substantial nontrivial even-order restricted-score learning profile, its complete five-type extremal edge-support classification, and a counterintuitive preservation of all eleven online query rounds when a vertex and six coordinates are deleted from the regular-seven realization. These are motivated structural and exact invariants, not arbitrary slices or a restatement of the known orientation-feasibility criterion.
